note: Where a browser client for a version can come from. An engine is a project that compiles (or reimplements) a Minecraft client for the web; this repository orchestrates them: it discovers versions, decides which engine can build one, and publishes what comes out. Adding an engine here is how a new version family becomes buildable.

engines.name: Gaius (TeaVM, official client bytecode)
engines.note: Compiles the official client jar to WebAssembly; one profile per version in port/versions/<version>.json. This is the engine for modern releases.

engines.name: EaglerPorts (TeaVM, classic versions)
engines.note: One repository per old version, each with its own offline WASM build. No compile step here: the release asset is the client.

engines.name: WebForge (CheerpJ, real JVM, real jars)
engines.note: A JVM in the page, so Forge jars load at runtime. Old versions only (Java 8-class library), but it is the one place where a .jar loads without a rebuild.

rules.release: Releases and snapshots are real client jars: buildable with an engine whose profile matches, otherwise they need a port.
rules.snapshot: Snapshots move weekly. A port needs its platform layer re-checked per snapshot, so they are catalogued and queued rather than built blindly.
rules.old_beta: Old versions have a different asset layout; use a classic engine.
